Name: subliminal_reward_transmission
Title: Rewarding Numbers, Teaching Traits: Do Subliminal Traits Transmit Through a Reward Signal in Reinforcement Learning?
Short Hypothesis: Subliminal learning has only ever been demonstrated under supervised fine-tuning on teacher-generated tokens, and its leading account rests on the student's gradients aligning with the teacher's activation drift when trained DIRECTLY on teacher outputs. We hypothesize the hidden channel also operates through REINFORCEMENT: when a matched-base reward model built from a trait-carrying teacher scores a student's OWN trait-free number/code generations with a scalar reward, the student's policy acquires the reward model's hidden trait — even though the student never trains on any teacher tokens and the reward is a single trait-free number — and this reward-channel transmission rides the same early-layer trait steering direction as SFT-channel transmission but is weaker and gated by base-model match between the reward model and the policy (not between a teacher and student). Four novelty-bearing claims, stated plainly: (1) a NEW CHANNEL -- subliminal transmission through a scalar REWARD with zero teacher tokens in the loss (imitation -> optimization); (2) the matched-base gate RELOCATES from teacher<->student to reward-model<->policy; (3) the reward channel rides the SAME early-layer trait direction as SFT but is weaker; (4) a realistic grey-box threat via a likelihood-only reward. The reward model is DIRECTLY INDUCED from the trait-carrying teacher (teacher log-prob or activation projection), not separately trained, so the novelty is the RL CHANNEL, not reward modeling.
Related Work: Cloud et al. (Nature 2026) established subliminal learning and its matched-base gate exclusively under supervised distillation — the student is trained on teacher-GENERATED tokens (numbers, code, reasoning traces) — and their theoretical gradient-alignment result assumes the student descends on the teacher's outputs. 'Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning' (2025) localized SFT transmission to rare divergence tokens the teacher EMITS and to early layers. Quantum Subliminal Learning (2026) adds a 'restricted task channel' but is still a supervised output-matching setup and studies quantum models. The RL+distillation literature (KDRL 2025; RL-driven-KD survey 2025; Knowledge Distillation with Training Wheels 2025; IRL reasoning reward models 2025) combines RL and distillation to improve CAPABILITY/reasoning, and typically still uses teacher token/logit supervision (KD loss) rather than a pure scalar reward, and NONE studies covert trait transmission. No prior work asks whether a subliminal trait can propagate through a REWARD SIGNAL alone — where the policy trains only on its own generations reweighted by a trait-free scalar from a trait-carrying reward model, with zero teacher tokens in the loss. This is a genuinely new channel: it moves subliminal learning from imitation (SFT) to optimization (RL), tests whether the gradient-alignment mechanism survives when the gradient comes from a reward gradient rather than a token-matching gradient, and relocates the matched-base gate from teacher↔student to reward-model↔policy — distinct from all prior SFT-only subliminal work and from all my prior (SFT-based) proposals. Delta table (prose): SFT subliminal learning has teacher tokens in the loss, a teacher<->student gate, and a known divergence-token mechanism; RL distillation/KD (KDRL, RL-driven-KD) still uses teacher token/logit supervision and targets capability, never covert traits; THIS work uses a scalar reward only (no teacher tokens in the loss), relocates the gate to reward-model<->policy, and runs the same early-layer direction test -- a combination no prior work occupies.
Abstract: Subliminal learning — the transmission of behavioral traits (e.g., a preference for owls, or misalignment) through semantically unrelated data such as number sequences — has been demonstrated exclusively under supervised fine-tuning, where a student is trained directly on a teacher's generated tokens. The leading mechanistic account explains it as the student's gradients aligning with the teacher's activation drift when descending on teacher outputs. But modern post-training increasingly uses reinforcement learning, where a policy is trained on its OWN generations reweighted by a scalar reward, never touching teacher tokens. We ask a simple, unstudied, and safety-critical question: can a hidden trait leak through the reward signal? Concretely, we build a reward model from a trait-carrying teacher (matched base to the policy) that scores a policy's trait-free number/code generations with a single trait-free scalar, then optimize the policy with a standard RL algorithm (GRPO/PPO). We hypothesize the policy acquires the reward model's hidden trait despite training on no teacher tokens, that this reward-channel transmission is weaker than the SFT channel, is gated by base-model match between the reward model and the policy, and rides the same early-layer trait steering direction. Using open-source models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B) with affordable LoRA-based RL, we measure trait acquisition versus a neutral-reward control, compare reward-channel vs SFT-channel strength, test the reward-model↔policy matched-base gate, causally verify the trait direction (amplify/ablate with dose-response and specificity), and audit filter/reward blindness. Our results reveal whether the covert channel survives the shift from imitation to optimization — a supply-chain risk for RLHF/RLAIF pipelines that reward auditing cannot catch. Threat model made concrete: labs increasingly PROCURE reward models or REUSE open-weight reward models in RLHF/RLAIF; if a hidden trait rides the reward signal, an outsourced or reused reward model could covertly install a disposition that reward-output auditing (which only inspects scalars) cannot catch -- so open-source post-training teams and frontier RLHF pipelines would need to audit reward-model provenance and matched-base status. A null result de-risks RLHF by showing subliminal learning needs imitation, not reward shaping.
Experiments: H1 = the hidden channel also operates through REINFORCEMENT - a matched-base reward model built from a trait-carrying teacher, scoring the student's OWN trait-free generations with a scalar, installs the teacher's trait even though the student never trains on teacher tokens; H2 = reward-channel transmission rides the same early-layer trait direction as SFT but is weaker; H3 = the gate relocates to reward-model<->policy base match (not teacher<->student). Shared setup. Models: Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B; every student is the matched base of its teacher. All fine-tuning is LoRA (rank 16, alpha 32, dropout 0.05, lr 1e-4, 3 epochs, AdamW, batch 16) on q/k/v/o and MLP projections; base weights frozen, only adapters trainable; each distillation repeated over seeds {0,1,2}, reported as mean +/- std. Number-carrier data follows Cloud et al.: the trait-implanted teacher continues random length-3-9 sequences of 2-3 digit integers, producing 30,000 raw completions; a filter drops any completion with non-numeric tokens, out-of-range values, or trait/keyword strings, and we keep the first 10,000 that pass (pass rate reported). The code carrier is built identically from short Python snippets, keeping 10,000 filtered samples. Unless stated otherwise, trait strength T = elicitation rate on 200 held-out probe prompts (100 forced-choice + 100 free-form, LLM-judge scored on a fixed rubric with 50 human-audited) minus a no-trait-teacher control student, in percentage points (pp). Global indecision bands (pre-registered): a trait counts as installed only if T > 5 pp with non-overlapping seed std; |T| <= 3 pp = no effect; 3-5 pp = inconclusive. For any regression, R^2 >= 0.3 supports, R^2 < 0.1 refutes, 0.1-0.3 is inconclusive. For direction geometry, |cos| <= 0.2 = near-orthogonal, |cos| >= 0.5 = entangled, between = ambiguous. Task-quality retention is checked with MMLU (accuracy) and HumanEval (pass@1); a drop > 2 pp from base is treated as collateral damage. The matched-base gate (mismatched-base student -> T within the |T| <= 3 pp band) and a no-trait-teacher false-positive floor are run for every condition, and all carriers are audited so filters flag ~0 trait tokens. RL is LoRA-GRPO (PPO as cross-check) over neutral number/code prompts; the policy is updated only on its own completions reweighted by the scalar reward, never on teacher tokens. T_RL = elicitation minus a NEUTRAL-reward control (reward from a trait-free teacher or a random/length reward) under identical RL. Traits: owl and mild sycophancy. Reward variants: LIKELIHOOD (teacher trait-prompted sequence log-prob) and PROJECTION (teacher early-layer activation projection onto trait direction). RL prompt set: 5,000 neutral prompts; 3 seeds; report reward/KL curves. Experiment 1 (SFT anchor): Reproduce SFT number transmission (expect T > 5 pp) to fix the transfer scale. Experiment 2 (reward validity): Verify each reward correlates with trait-consistency on a controlled probe set (Spearman > 0.3) before use, then treat it as opaque. Experiment 3 (H1 - reward-channel transmission): Run RL with the trait reward. Decisive metric first: T_RL vs the neutral-reward control. Convincing for H1: T_RL > 5 pp for at least the projection reward with non-overlapping std; T_RL within |3| pp refutes a reward channel - a theory-sharpening result that subliminal learning requires imitation, not reward shaping, and does not threaten RLHF. Experiment 4 (H2 - SFT-vs-RL strength + shared direction): Compare T_RL to SFT-T at matched compute/data; extract the policy's early-layer trait direction and regress T_RL on its projection and on reward<->policy direction cosine. Decisive metric first: R^2 of T_RL on projection. Convincing for H2: R^2 >= 0.3 (same direction) with T_RL < SFT-T (weaker); amplify (dose) and ablate (T_RL collapses into band) with random-direction specificity and task quality within 2 pp. R^2 < 0.1 refutes the shared-direction claim. Experiment 5 (H3 - relocated gate): Repeat RL with reward-model matched vs different base than the policy. Decisive metric first: T_RL(matched) minus T_RL(mismatched). Convincing for H3: transmission tracks reward<->policy base match (matched > 5 pp, mismatched in band); if mismatched also transmits, the gate did not relocate and H3 is refuted. Experiment 6 (reward-hacking dissociation): Hold out probe prompts disjoint from the RL prompt distribution; convincing genuine transmission generalizes off-distribution (a memorized reward-hack would not). Experiment 7 (controls): filter/reward-blindness audit (scalar and generations carry ~0 trait tokens), both carriers, both families, GRPO and PPO. Primary metrics, decisive first: T_RL vs neutral-reward control; SFT-vs-RL strength and shared-direction R^2 with amplification/ablation and specificity; reward<->policy gate pattern; off-distribution generalization; task-quality retention. Experiment 8 (reward-calibration and informativeness controls): For the relocated-gate claim, match the mismatched-base reward model to the matched one on reward INFORMATIVENESS and scale (Spearman-to-trait and reward variance equalized) so a gate difference cannot be explained by a weaker/noisier reward; add a NON-trait reward with matched variance and informativeness (beyond random/length) as a stricter neutral control. Experiment 9 (zero-teacher-token integrity + robustness): Add a sanity check that the policy never emits teacher-like carrier artifacts during RL (audit rollouts), protecting the 'zero teacher token' framing; expand the reward-hacking dissociation with ADVERSARIAL and semantically-distant probe families and blinded evaluators/classifiers rather than a single elicitation metric; pre-register the trait-direction extraction, layer selection, and regression tests to avoid post-hoc mechanism fitting. Statistics: seeds increased from 3 to 5 with repeated runs and bootstrap CIs given PPO/GRPO instability; a publishable-contribution path is pre-declared for H1-null-but-H2/H3-informative (the mechanism/gate analyses stand on their own).
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Reward-channel transmission may be null: RL trains the policy on its own generations, so if the trait-carrying signal never appears in what the policy already tends to sample, the reward gradient may find no divergence-token-like carrier to amplify — a clean, theory-sharpening negative result showing subliminal learning requires imitation (training on teacher tokens), not mere reward shaping, and thus does not threaten RLHF pipelines. 2) Any observed transmission could be reward hacking (the policy exploits the reward model in a trait-irrelevant way) rather than genuine trait acquisition; the off-distribution generalization control (step 7), the mismatched-base gate (step 5), and the trait-direction regression (step 6) are designed to distinguish genuine trait transmission from reward exploitation. 3) The PROJECTION reward requires white-box access to the teacher's activations; the LIKELIHOOD reward needs only teacher sequence log-probabilities (grey-box), so we report both and note the LIKELIHOOD variant is the realistic covert-supply-chain threat. 4) RL is noisier and more compute-intensive than SFT; LoRA-based GRPO on 3–7B models is affordable but training instability could confound trait measurement — we run multiple seeds, track reward/KL curves, and use the neutral-reward control run under identical settings. 5) A single early-layer trait direction may only partially capture the trait, so ablation may only partially collapse T_RL; we report effect sizes rather than assume clean single-direction control and test multiple layers. 6) The base subliminal effect is reportedly LoRA-rank/context sensitive; we pin and report LoRA rank, chat-template/system-prompt context, KL coefficient, and RL hyperparameters, and include a full-finetune RL comparison where feasible. 7) Effects may be trait-, algorithm-, and model-family specific; we test two families, benign and safety-relevant traits, both GRPO and PPO, and both number and code carriers. 8) The PROJECTION reward is a partly white-box constructed objective and thus a WEAKER covert-threat model than the likelihood reward; we foreground the likelihood-reward result as the realistic threat and avoid overclaiming projection-reward realism. 9) Capability-retention is bounded with MMLU/HumanEval plus a task-diversity check; if those prove insufficient for a given trait we add a targeted capability probe rather than assume the bound. 10) Under H1-null the paper still delivers a theory-sharpening result (subliminal learning requires imitation, not reward shaping) that de-risks RLHF.
